A sourdough starter is a mix of flour and water that collects wild yeast and lactic acid bacteria. Once it is lively, it can raise bread on its own. It takes about a week to get going and only a few minutes a day after that.

== Ingredients ==
* Whole wheat or rye flour, for the first few days
* Unbleached white bread flour
* Lukewarm water (filtered, or tap water left out overnight)
* A clean glass jar of about 1 litre, with a loose lid
* A rubber band to mark the level

== Method ==
# '''Day 1:''' Stir 50 g whole wheat flour and 50 g water in the jar until no dry flour remains. Cover loosely and leave at room temperature (21 to 25 °C).
# '''Day 2:''' You may see nothing at all. That is normal. Stir it once and leave it alone.
# '''Days 3 to 7:''' Once a day, discard all but 50 g, then add 50 g white flour and 50 g water. Mark the level with the rubber band.
# The starter is ready when it reliably doubles within 4 to 8 hours of feeding, smells pleasantly sour and is full of bubbles.
# '''Keeping it:''' Feed it daily at room temperature, or keep it in the fridge and feed it once a week.

== Troubleshooting ==
* '''Grey liquid on top''' means the starter is hungry. Pour it off or stir it in, then feed.
* '''Lots of bubbles on day 2, then nothing''' is common. The early bubbles come from bacteria that die off. Keep feeding and the yeast takes over.
* '''Fuzzy mould, or pink or orange streaks''': throw the whole starter away, wash the jar and start again. Do not try to rescue it.

== Tips ==
* Weigh rather than measure by cups. Small differences matter at this scale.
* A warm spot, such as the oven with only the light on, speeds things up. Check the temperature first.
* The feeding ratio sets the timing. At 1:1:1 (starter, flour, water) it peaks in about 4 hours at room temperature, at 1:5:5 in about 12.
* Use the discard in [[Buttermilk pancakes]].

See also: [[Herb focaccia]].
